exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Variance of a Sum or Difference of Independent Random Variables

question.text: For two independent random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\textrm{Var}[X]=7$ and $\textrm{Var}[Y]=9.$ Find $\textrm{Var}[Y-X].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables, then

\[ \textrm{Var}[Y\pm X]=\textrm{Var}[Y]+\textrm{Var}[X]. \]

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

\[ \textrm{Var}[Y-X]= 9+7 = 16. \]

question.text: For two independent random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\textrm{Var}[X]=11$ and $\textrm{Var}[Y]=15.$ Find $\textrm{Var}\left[2X-3Y\right].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent variables, and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$ \textrm{Var}[aX+bY]=a^2\textrm{Var}[X]+b^2\textrm{Var}[Y]. $$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$ \textrm{Var}\left[2X-3Y\right]=\left(2\right)^2\cdot 11+\left(-3\right)^2\cdot 15 =179. $$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Combined Variance Given Some Raw Moments

question.text:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(x)$ $0.3$ $0.6$ $0.1$

$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $0.3$ $0.4$ $0.3$

Find $\textrm{Var}[5X-4Y].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+bY]=a^2\textrm{Var}[X]+b^2\textrm{Var}[Y]. \]

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula $$ \textrm {Var}[X]=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2. $$

First, let's find $\textrm{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_X$, then

\begin{align} \textrm E[X]&=\sum_{x\in S_X} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.6+2\cdot 0.1\\[5pt] &=0.8 \end{align}

and

\begin{align} \textrm E[X^2]&=\sum_{x\in S_X} x^2\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.6+4\cdot 0.1\\[5pt] &=1. \end{align}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2\\[5pt] &= 1 - 0.8^2\\[5pt] &=0.36. \end{align*}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_Y$, then

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y]&=\sum_{y\in S_Y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.3\\[5pt] &=1 \end{align}

and

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y^2]&=\sum_{y\in S_Y} y^2\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.4+4\cdot 0.3\\[5pt] &=1.6. \end{align}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[Y] &= \textrm E[Y^2] - \textrm E[Y]^2\\[5pt] &= 1.6 - 1^2\\[5pt] &=0.6. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\begin{align} \textrm{Var}[5X-4Y] &= 5^2\textrm{Var}[X]+(-4)^2\textrm{Var}[Y] \\[5pt] &=25(0.36)+16(0.6)\\[5pt] &=18.6. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating a Combined Variance Given Some Raw Moments

question.text: Consider two independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ with expectations $\textrm E[X]=2$, $\textrm E[Y]=4$ and second raw moments $\textrm E[X^2]=5$ and $\textrm E[Y^2]=23.$ Find the variance of $5X+7Y.$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+bY]=a^2\textrm{Var}[X]+b^2\textrm{Var}[Y]. \]

Also, the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula $$ \textrm {Var}[X]=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2. $$

First, let's find $\textrm{Var}[X]\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \textrm {Var}[X] &=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2\\[5pt] &=\textrm 5-\textrm 2^2\\[5pt] &=1. \end{align*}

Similarly,

\begin{align*} \textrm {Var}[Y] &=\textrm E[Y^2]-\textrm E[Y]^2\\[5pt] &=\textrm 23-\textrm 4^2\\[5pt] &=7. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align} \textrm{Var}[5X+7Y]&=5^2\textrm{Var}[X]+7^2\textrm{Var}[Y]\\[5pt] &=25(1)+49(7)\\[5pt] &=368. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating a Combined Variance Given Some Raw Moments

question.text:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $10$ $15$ $20$ $25$
$f(x)$ $0.25$ $0.35$ $0.15$ $0.25$

$y$ $12$ $18$
$f(y)$ $0.33$ $0.67$

Find $\textrm{Var}[1.5X+2Y].$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+bY]=a^2\textrm{Var}[X]+b^2\textrm{Var}[Y]. \]

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula $$ \textrm {Var}[X]=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2. $$

First, let's find $\textrm{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_X$, then

\begin{align} \textrm E[X]&=\sum_{x\in S_X} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=10\cdot 0.25+15\cdot 0.35+20\cdot 0.15+25\cdot 0.25\\[5pt] &=17 \end{align}

and

\begin{align} \textrm E[X^2]&=\sum_{x\in S_X} x^2\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=100\cdot 0.25+225\cdot 0.35+400\cdot 0.15+625\cdot 0.25\\[5pt] &=320. \end{align}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2\\[5pt] &= 320 - 17^2\\[5pt] &=31. \end{align*}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_Y$, then

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y]&=\sum_{y\in S_Y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=12\cdot 0.33+18\cdot 0.67\\[5pt] &=16.02 \end{align}

and

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y^2]&=\sum_{y\in S_Y} y^2\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=144\cdot 0.33+324\cdot 0.67\\[5pt] &=264.6. \end{align}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[Y] &= \textrm E[Y^2] - \textrm E[Y]^2\\[5pt] &= 264.6 - 16.02^2\\[5pt] &=7.9596. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\begin{align} \textrm{Var}[1.5X+2Y] &= 1.5^2\textrm{Var}[X]+2^2\textrm{Var}[Y] \\[5pt] &=2.25(31)+4(7.9596)\\[5pt] &\approx 101.59. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating a Combined Variance Given Some Raw Moments

question.text: Consider two independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ with expectations $\textrm E[X]=2.4,$ $\textrm E[Y]=3.5$ and second raw moments $\textrm E[X^2]=12$ and $\textrm E[Y^2]=17.$ Find the variance of $5X-2Y.$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+bY]=a^2\textrm{Var}[X]+b^2\textrm{Var}[Y]. \]

Also, the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula $$ \textrm {Var}[X]=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2. $$

First, let's find $\textrm{Var}[X]\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \textrm {Var}[X] &=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2\\[5pt] &= 12- 2.4^2\\[5pt] &=6.24. \end{align*}

Similarly,

\begin{align*} \textrm {Var}[Y] &=\textrm E[Y^2]-\textrm E[Y]^2\\[5pt] &= 17- 3.5^2\\[5pt] &=4.75. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align} \textrm{Var}\left[5X-2Y\right]&=5^2\textrm{Var}[X]+(-2)^2\textrm{Var}[Y]\\[5pt] &=25\left(6.24\right)+4\left(4.75\right)\\[5pt] &=175. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating a Combined Variance Given Some Raw Moments

question.text:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(x)$ $\dfrac 13$ $\dfrac 13$ $\dfrac 13$

$y$ $2$ $4$ $6$
$f(y)$ $\dfrac 12$ $\dfrac 14$ $\dfrac 14$

Find $\textrm{Var}[3X-2Y].$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+bY]=a^2\textrm{Var}[X]+b^2\textrm{Var}[Y]. \]

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula $$ \textrm {Var}[X]=\textrm E[X^2]-\textrm E[X]^2. $$

First, let's find $\textrm{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_X$, then

\begin{align} \textrm E[X]&=\sum_{x\in S_X} x\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0\left(\dfrac 13\right)+1\left(\dfrac 13\right)+2\left(\dfrac 13\right)\\[5pt] &=1 \end{align}

and

\begin{align} \textrm E[X^2]&=\sum_{x\in S_X} x^2\cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0^2\cdot\left(\dfrac 13\right)+1^2\cdot\left(\dfrac 13\right)+2^2\cdot\left(\dfrac 13\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac 53. \end{align}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 53 - 1^2\\[5pt] &=\dfrac 23. \end{align*}

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_Y$, then

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y]&=\sum_{y\in S_Y} y\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=2\left(\dfrac 12\right)+4\left(\dfrac 14\right)+6\left(\dfrac 14\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac 72 \end{align}

and

\begin{align} \textrm E[Y^2]&=\sum_{y\in S_Y} y^2\cdot f(y)\\[5pt] &=2^2\cdot\left(\dfrac 12\right)+4^2\cdot\left(\dfrac 14\right)+6^2\cdot\left(\dfrac 14\right)\\[5pt] &=15. \end{align}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[Y] &= \textrm E[Y^2] - \textrm E[Y]^2\\[5pt] &= 15- \left(\dfrac 72\right)^2\\[5pt] &=\dfrac {11}{4}. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\begin{align} \textrm{Var}[3X-2Y] &= 3^2\textrm{Var}[X]+(-2)^2\textrm{Var}[Y] \\[5pt] &=9\cdot \dfrac 23+4\cdot\dfrac {11}{4} \\[5pt] &=17. \end{align}
